items.title: Repair the tiny-home cost calculator around honest quote-first and partial-result states
items.baseline: The live calculator ranks as a real indexed tool but submits an all-blank form as a $0 estimated all-in budget and turns an $85,000 quote with every other major bucket blank into a $102,000 estimated all-in budget. The form also risks utility double counting, does not distinguish blank from an explicit zero, lacks project-type context, delays the tool behind a large limits panel, and routes cost readers to weak default local-page follow-ups.
items.hypothesis: A quote-first calculator that keeps unknown, added amount including typed zero, already covered, and not applicable distinct; labels partial totals honestly; separates utility buckets; adapts verification prompts to the project path; and puts missing-cost decisions before any incomplete subtotal will help cautious buyers compare a quote without inventing national-average costs.
items.expected_effect: The existing indexed URL becomes a clearer buyer-protection tool for quote and budget reality checking, with testable blank, partial, resolved-input, financing, and four-state behavior and no implied typical or complete price.
items.success_signal: Current query/SERP and representative ranking-page research is durable; blank input never produces a dollar result; partial inputs never produce an all-in claim; unknown, added amount including typed zero, already covered, and not applicable remain distinct; utility fields cannot double count a general hookup bucket; beginner, intermediate, and advanced quote/budget personas pass; every visible block has a distinct purpose; native, browser, production, and independent review gates pass.
